correctness.rationale: Degree-d finite continued fractions with degree-one partial quotients T or T+1 correspond bijectively to 2^d binary continuant words. The recurrence K_j=a_j K_{j-1}+K_{j-2} is exact, denominator degree j and uniqueness follows from the Euclidean algorithm. Beyond the source 6+66 candidate calculation, an independently written C11 full census counted every 2^d word at each d=1,...,26 without depending on Blackburn factor restrictions; all degrees<=25 have max multiplicity <=64, and at degree26 precisely one denominator has multiplicity128, mask123935485. Independent GF2 product of all seven displayed factors equals 123935485. Exhaustion is a complete finite proof of the stated first-degree property; it does not extrapolate to higher degrees.
